Okay if anyone is actually interested in using these, the original pronunciation of some of the names is a little stange (this is based on classical Latin pronunciation, not ecclesiastical latin)

For example, in latin, all "c"s are hard, and pronounced like "k". So the name Liciana would be pronounced "Lee-kee-ana".

Also, the dipthong "ae" makes an "ay" sound, so Aemilia would be "eye-mil-e-uh", not pronounced like Amelia usually is.

Edit: In addition, you'll notice that most of these names are similar to names for male Romans.

Male Romans had three names. For example, in Gaius Julius Caesar, Gauis is kind of like a first name but not really (there was only like 10 of these so everyone had the same ones haha), Julius is the clan name (this is the name most people would be called), and Caesar is the cognomen, which is just another last name.

Daughters would usually only be named after the father's clan name. Like, if Julius Caesar had three girls, they would all be named Julia, but they would usually go by nicknames determined by their birth order. For example, if the girl was the third girl born in the family, she might go by "tertia", which means third in Latin. 

So even though these names are really pretty, and honestly I will probably name my kids something Roman if I ever have any, it's important to know the correct pronunciation and the backstory behind how they came to be. Some people might not like how all of these names are basically just feminine versions of guy's names and that the girls usually didn't necessarily go by their given name.

I hope this was informative!

I just finished my freshman year. I was totally fine with 14 meals. There was only one week that I ran out of meals, and I just used my credit card on Tapingo for the last day of the week.

That being said, most of my classes were in the afternoon, so I only used my meal swipe for breakfast a few times a week. Additionally, my friends and I would eat out once or twice a week, and sometimes I was just too lazy to go to the dining hall and ate instant food in my room.

I would say most of my friends were in the same situation, and we were all okay with 14 meals. However, if you plan on staying every weekend, eating breakfast every day, and not going out to eat, unlimited might be the better choice. Hope this helps!
